root_cause.text: The QRTR nameservice (`net/qrtr/ns.c`) did not enforce any per-node bound on `qrtr_node->servers` when processing `NEW_SERVER` messages, allowing a malicious client to create unbounded server entries and exhaust kernel memory.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `u32 server_count` to `struct qrtr_node`, defines `QRTR_NS_MAX_SERVERS 256`, and in `server_add()` rejects new entries when `!old && node->server_count >= QRTR_NS_MAX_SERVERS`, which directly matches the CVE note that “Current code does no bound checking on the number of servers added per node” and that flooding `NEW_SERVER` messages could “exhaust memory.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Add per-node server counting support and define a maximum server limit for QRTR namespace handling.
intent_record.what: A new u32 field named server_count was added to struct qrtr_node, and a new macro QRTR_NS_MAX_SERVERS was introduced with the value 256 along with a comment describing it as the maximum server limit.
intent_record.how: This change prepares qrtr_node to track how many servers are associated with a node and establishes a fixed upper bound for the number of servers that can be handled, enabling later code to enforce that limit or count servers explicitly.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add node validation and enforce the per-node QRTR server limit before creating a new server entry.
intent_record.what: The function now acquires a node reference with `node_get(node_id)` and returns `NULL` if no node is found. It then looks up any existing server entry for `port` with `xa_load(&node->servers, port)`, and if there is no existing entry and `node->server_count` has reached `QRTR_NS_MAX_SERVERS`, it logs a rate-limited error and returns `NULL` before allocating the new server object.
intent_record.how: At runtime, server creation is now blocked when the target node does not exist or when adding a new server would exceed the per-node maximum server limit. Existing servers on the same port are not counted against this limit check, so the code prevents uncontrolled growth of server registrations while allowing updates or reuse of an already-registered port.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove an unnecessary node lookup and null-check in server_add so the server can be inserted using the existing node reference.
intent_record.what: The diff removes the call to `node_get(node_id)` and its associated null-check and error jump from `server_add()`, so the function no longer fetches `node` at that point before calling `xa_store(&node->servers, port, srv, GFP_KERNEL)`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, `server_add()` now assumes `node` is already available in scope and proceeds directly to store the new server entry in the node's server table. This eliminates the early failure path that would have aborted if `node_get()` returned NULL.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix server accounting in server_add() by incrementing node->server_count on the missing add path.
intent_record.what: In the non-error path of server_add(), an else branch was added after the existing conditional so that node->server_count is incremented when the earlier condition is not taken.
intent_record.how: This changes runtime accounting for QRTR servers by ensuring the node's server_count is updated for the alternate add path, preventing the count from staying stale when a server is added without entering the prior branch.

intent_record.intent_summary: Decrement the node server count when a server is removed to keep accounting accurate.
intent_record.what: In `server_del()`, a new statement `node->server_count--;` was added immediately after `kfree(srv);` and before returning 0.
intent_record.how: When a server is deleted, the per-node server count is now decremented at runtime, keeping the count in sync with the actual number of registered servers and preventing it from remaining artificially high after removals.

intent_record.intent_summary: Rate-limit repeated error logs in `qrtr_ns_worker()` to avoid flooding the kernel log.
intent_record.what: In `qrtr_ns_worker()`, the error logging call inside the `ret < 0` path was changed from `pr_err(...)` to `pr_err_ratelimited(...)` while keeping the same format string and arguments.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function will now suppress repeated error messages when this failure happens frequently, reducing log spam while still reporting the error periodically.

Add node validation and enforce the per-node QRTR server limit before creating a new server entry.
Remove an unnecessary node lookup and null-check in server_add so the server can be inserted using the existing node reference.
Fix server accounting in server_add() by incrementing node->server_count on the missing add path.
Decrement the node server count when a server is removed to keep accounting accurate.
Rate-limit repeated error logs in `qrtr_ns_worker()` to avoid flooding the kernel log.

relevance_review.reason: The change adds per-node server counting and a maximum server limit in QRTR namespace handling, which directly addresses the root cause of unbounded `qrtr_node->servers` growth from `NEW_SERVER` messages and the resulting memory exhaustion.

The change directly addresses the root cause by validating the node and enforcing a per-node limit on qrtr_node->servers before accepting NEW_SERVER messages, preventing unbounded server entry creation and memory exhaustion.

The change is a refactor in server_add to reuse an existing node reference and remove a lookup/null-check. It does not add any per-node limit or bound on qrtr_node->servers, nor address unbounded NEW_SERVER entry creation or memory exhaustion.

The root cause is unbounded growth of qrtr_node->servers from NEW_SERVER processing. Fixing server accounting in server_add() by incrementing node->server_count on the add path is directly related to enforcing per-node server tracking and preventing uncontrolled server entry accumulation.

The vulnerability is caused by unbounded growth of qrtr_node->servers from NEW_SERVER handling. Decrementing the server count on removal is part of the accounting needed to enforce or maintain per-node limits, so this change is directly related to the root cause.

The change only rate-limits error logging in qrtr_ns_worker(); it does not add any bound or validation on qrtr_node->servers when handling NEW_SERVER messages, so it does not address the unbounded server-entry memory exhaustion issue.

candidates.rationale: This allocation creates a new server entry for each NEW_SERVER message, and in the vulnerable code it could proceed without any per-node limit check, enabling unbounded growth of qrtr_node->servers and memory exhaustion.

vuln_statements.explanation: This allocation creates a new server entry on each NEW_SERVER message. In the vulnerable code, it occurred without enforcing any per-node limit on qrtr_node->servers, allowing an attacker to trigger unbounded server creation and exhaust kernel memory.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown diff only changes allocation call sites from `kzalloc_obj(*node, GFP_KERNEL)` / `kzalloc_obj(*srv, GFP_KERNEL)` / `kzalloc_obj(*lookup, GFP_KERNEL)` to `kzalloc_obj(*node)` etc. There is no logic here related to processing `NEW_SERVER` messages, no per-node `qrtr_node->servers` bound checking, and no server-entry limit enforcement. Therefore the vulnerable construct described in the root cause is absent from this snippet, and this commit does not show any fix for that issue.
